body.estimand_functional: Candidate critical inference target: \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J,\quad\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))\Rightarrow N(0,V(P))\); the Gaussian arrow remains conditional on discharging oeq:uniform-critical-control.

sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the declared high-order signed periodized KDE followed by clipping and mass normalization.  Both map derivatives and covariance scores must solve an augmented scalar--harmonic system: a mean-zero elliptic equation and a two-dimensional weighted-Hodge stationarity equation.  Opposite-fold pilots feed the corresponding adjoint solves, and the declared ridge totalizes every reported block inverse.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

body.tldr: The note proves intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes identification and derives the full translation-aware nested derivative through a uniformly coercive weighted-Hodge Schur complement.  The derivation corrects the frozen harmonic formula by retaining the inner and outer coefficient-divergence correctors.  The generic variable-coefficient critical covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint ellipses, and class-uniform upper risk remain conditional on the open transformed-kernel and moving-pole estimates.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-source transport linearizations neither determine torus harmonic translations for two varying endpoints nor control singular shrinking-bandwidth scores for a generated target.  The weighted-Hodge argument closes the first gap under the maintained assumptions; uniform critical score stability remains open.
project_justification.niche: The selected translation is determined by reduced-cost stationarity.  Its Hessian is a weighted-Hodge energy that is uniformly coercive from density positivity and transport ellipticity.  After both augmented systems are solved, nesting still reduces the singular part to one outer Green response to four independent noises.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the corrected augmented derivative, its bounded adjoint harmonic scores, intrinsic identification, and analytic benchmark laws.  It leaves the general-density covariance and inference package behind the explicit uniform transformed-kernel, moving-pole, fourth-moment, and mixed nonlinear remainder obligations.

body.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC supplies the Euclidean multivariate changes-in-changes identification motivation, while this note separately proves its intrinsic full-support flat-torus identification.  GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization treats a fixed-source density curve and does not provide the two-endpoint weighted-Hodge harmonic system derived here.  ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the critical two-dimensional pointwise limit only in the fixed-source uniform case.  Neither source proves the still-open variable-coefficient transformed-score and moving-pole bounds needed for the nested inference claims.
body.interpretation: At each prespecified treated-post location, the estimand is the selected-lift no-treatment displacement.  Translation uncertainty is not set to zero: it is recovered from a two-dimensional reduced-cost stationarity equation and propagated through the generated target.  These harmonic terms are bounded-order, whereas the candidate logarithmic variance is generated by the four independent scalar Green responses.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected derivative is deterministic and translation-aware, but the critical statistical module remains open.  In particular, no current proof uniformly replaces nonlinear transformed KDE scores with frozen-pole responses, controls estimated poles at bandwidth scale, or integrates the mixed remainder on clipping and lift-fallback events.  The fixed-grid, positivity, ellipticity, branch-separation, and independent-sample restrictions remain in force.
body.honest_scope: The proved root calculation concerns smooth positive four-cell laws on the flat torus and selected no-cut transport branches.  It does not yet certify the displayed covariance estimator, multiplier coverage, or class-uniform plug-in risk.  Applying the proposal to Card--Krueger data additionally requires a prespecified smooth bivariate periodic outcome construction, a defensible independent-cell sampling approximation, and numerical errors below the eventual critical statistical scales.
